submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent: 1.88 uA at Ca 0.314 / Mn 0.686. That is near marokite CaMn2O4, which MACE puts on the hull and MEGNet gives a 2.54 eV HSE gap, so it can absorb the 3.22 eV light. Photocurrent went up steadily from Ca 0.398 (0.39 uA) to 0.338 (1.74 uA) to 0.314 (1.88 uA).

rejected.reason: Measured 0.39 uA near Ca2Mn3O8; lower than the samples closer to marokite.
The expected phases there, CaMnO3 (0.19 eV) and Ca3Mn2O7 (0.29 eV), are predicted near-metallic. Not measured.
The expected phases there, CaMn3O6 (0.33 eV), CaMn7O12 (0.82 eV) and Mn3O4 (0.94 eV), have small predicted gaps. Not measured, so a higher value there can't be ruled out.

consultations.verdict: Support: Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca 0.4) has predicted HSE gap 2.69 eV, below 3.22 eV photon energy but not metallic, unlike CaMnO3 (0.19) and Ca3Mn2O7 (0.29). Index 23 (Ca 0.398) sits on that stoichiometry.
Support: marokite CaMn2O4 is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom) and MEGNet HSE gap 2.54 eV absorbs at 3.22 eV; index 8 (Ca 0.338) is close to its stoichiometry.

Mixed/against going far Mn-rich: CaMn3O6 (0.33 eV) and Mn3O4 (0.94 eV) are predicted small-gap, so compositions well past Ca 0.33 dilute the 2.5 eV marokite absorber. Measured trend (Ca 0.398: 0.39 uA -> Ca 0.338: 1.74 uA) rises toward marokite, so index 10 (Ca 0.314), just on the Mn-rich side of CaMn2O4, is the best last probe.
